    70	For implementation tasks, do not edit docs as a start gate. Read what is useful, finish the implementation and
    71	risk-matched validation, then have the main Agent launch one asynchronous docs SubAgent:
    72	
    73	1. the main Agent supplies the final behavior summary, changed files, validation results, and candidate owners;
    74	2. one docs SubAgent identifies the durable facts that changed;
    75	3. that SubAgent patches the smallest owning document once;
    76	4. it updates an INDEX or OVERVIEW only when navigation changed;
    77	5. it checks affected links and stops.
    78	
    79	The docs SubAgent is the only writer for that maintenance pass. The main Agent should not wait for ancillary docs work
    80	or modify the same docs concurrently. If no SubAgent is available, the main Agent performs the same single lightweight
    81	pass at the end.
    82	
    83	Do not persist session plans, intermediate reasoning, raw command output, review transcripts, or temporary status.
    84	If nothing durable changed, do not modify docs.
    85	
    86	For a docs-only organization task, first finish the inventory and target shape, then apply one coherent patch rather
    87	than repeatedly rewriting the tree while exploring.
    88	
    89	## Feature Docs
    90	
    91	Use one directory per durable feature only when a directory helps navigation. A small feature may be represented by
    92	a single README.
    93	
    94	Recommended README sections, chosen as needed rather than copied mechanically:
    95	
    96	- purpose and scope;
    97	- current behavior;
    98	- important interfaces or data shapes;
    99	- constraints and known limitations;
   100	- concise current status or next step;
   101	- links to stable supporting references.
   102	
   103	Use `assets/feature-template/` as a starting point, then remove unused sections. An `INDEX.md` inside the feature is
   104	only useful when the feature has several stable leaf documents.
   105	
   106	## Reference Docs
   107	
   108	Put cross-feature, relatively stable knowledge under `docs/reference/`, for example:
   109	
   110	- architecture and dependency direction;
   111	- public or external interfaces;
   112	- configuration and operational runbooks;
   113	- project-wide validation commands.
   114	
   115	Feature-specific details stay in the Feature README. Avoid copying the same status or interface description into
   116	OVERVIEW, indexes, feature docs, and references.
   117	
   118	## Navigation
   119	
   120	Top-level files are maps, not summaries of everything below them:
   121	
   122	- `AGENTS.md` contains stable rules and an optional context link;
   123	- `OVERVIEW.md` names major modules and where to go next;
   124	- an INDEX explains which document to open for which task;
   125	- a leaf contains the actual knowledge.
   126	
   127	Use links that work in the target repository. Parent links are helpful for deep leaves but are not required on every
   128	small document when navigation is already obvious.
   129	
   130	## Mainline Routes
   131	
   132	Most projects need only a short current-focus or next-step note in the owning README. Use a route document only when
   133	several workstreams, dependencies, or handoffs must survive across sessions. Prefer semantic names and readable text;
   134	do not introduce machine node IDs, mandatory DAG manifests, or multi-axis status schemas unless the project already
   135	needs them.
   136	
   137	## Migration
   138	
   139	1. Inventory existing Markdown and identify the actual entrypoints.
   140	2. Keep the documents that carry stable, useful knowledge.

     4	  Lightweight docs-only intake for adding a product or engineering idea to a harness-managed repository.
     5	  Use when the user invokes add-idea or asks to record and route an idea to a new or existing Feature.
     6	  Inspect current owners, ask only the most important unresolved product or hard-boundary question, then
     7	  update the smallest set of core docs once. Do not produce Specs, questionnaires, or code.
     8	disable-model-invocation: true
     9	---
    10	
    11	# Add Idea
    12	
    13	Use this skill to turn an idea into a clear Feature owner and a small durable documentation update. The outcome is
    14	not a complete implementation plan.
    15	
    16	Read [references/routing-contract.md](references/routing-contract.md) before choosing the owner. Use
    17	[`../progressive-disclosure-docs/references/core-docs-guide.md`](../progressive-disclosure-docs/references/core-docs-guide.md)
    18	for document placement.
    19	
    20	## Interaction Rules
    21	
    22	- Preserve the user's intended outcome instead of expanding the process around it.
    23	- Discover repository facts yourself; do not ask the user to locate files or repeat known context.
    24	- Ask only when the answer changes the product outcome, Feature ownership, or a hard safety/authorization/compatibility
    25	  boundary.
    26	- Ask one compact question about the most consequential unknown and include a recommended default.
    27	- Do not run a checklist interview. Scope details, acceptance wording, file layout, test shape, rollout mechanics, and
    28	  other reversible implementation choices can remain open unless they are the actual decision the user brought.
    29	- If the request and repository are clear enough, skip Grill entirely.
    30	- Do not require a separate confirmation ceremony after restating information the user already supplied.
    31	
    32	When the user explicitly says "grill me", ask for the single most important missing decision first. Continue asking only
    33	if the answer exposes another genuine blocker; do not walk a predetermined questionnaire.
    34	
    35	## Workflow
    36	
    37	### 1. Find the likely owner
    38	
    39	Read progressively:
    40	
    41	1. root `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` if present;
    42	2. `docs/OVERVIEW.md` and `docs/feature/INDEX.md` if present;
    43	3. at most the likely owning Feature README(s);
    44	4. targeted code or references only when they settle ownership.
    45	
    46	Prefer an existing Feature when it already owns the user-visible responsibility. A new phrase or implementation detail
    47	is not by itself a new Feature.
    48	
    49	### 2. Apply the minimal clarity check
    50	
    51	An idea is clear enough when you can state:
    52	
    53	- the desired outcome;
    54	- the broad in-scope boundary;
    55	- the likely Feature owner;
    56	- any hard constraint that must not be crossed.
    57	
    58	An exact acceptance matrix, module map, API shape, migration plan, test plan, rollback plan, or full non-goal list is not
    59	required at intake. Leave those choices to implementation unless the user is deciding them now.
    60	
    61	If one core item remains ambiguous, ask one question. If the ambiguity is safely reversible, state the assumption and
    62	continue.
    63	
    64	### 3. Choose the route
    65	
    66	Choose one owner route:
    67	
    68	- `PATCH_FEATURE`: an existing Feature owns the outcome;
    69	- `CREATE_FEATURE`: the idea has an independent durable outcome or ownership boundary;
    70	- `BLOCKED_OWNER`: choosing an owner would redefine a product or safety boundary without user direction.
    71	
    72	Choose the smallest docs route:
    73	
    74	- `FEATURE_README_PATCH`: update the owning README with the stable idea boundary;
    75	- `NAVIGATION_PATCH`: create/register a new Feature or repair a route;
    76	- `NO_DOC_CHANGE`: the idea is too transient, already documented, or only a reversible local detail.
    77	
    78	Do not create requirements, Spec, ADR, changelog, task board, interview transcript, or parallel idea backlog as part of
    79	this skill. Preserve an existing project convention when it already requires one, but do not introduce it from the harness.
    80	
    81	### 4. Apply one documentation patch
    82	
    83	After ownership and the core boundary are clear, update docs once:
    84	
    85	- for `PATCH_FEATURE`, add the smallest useful section or bullets to the existing Feature README;
    86	- for `CREATE_FEATURE`, copy the lightweight Feature README template, remove unused sections, and register it only in
    87	  the indexes that actually exist;
    88	- update `OVERVIEW.md` only when project-level navigation changes;
    89	- keep implementation detail out of the intake document.
    90	
    91	Do not alternate between questions and file writes. Gather the one necessary answer first, then make one coherent patch.
    92	
    93	### 5. Finish briefly
    94	
    95	Report:
    96	
    97	- selected owner and why;
    98	- the core boundary recorded;
    99	- files updated, or why no docs changed;
   100	- the next practical step.
   101	
   102	This skill does not implement code. A later implementation request can proceed directly through the repository's normal
   103	workflow without first creating more harness artifacts.
   104	
   105	## Stop Conditions
   106	
   107	Stop and surface one decision when:
   108	
   109	- two owners remain equally plausible and the choice changes product behavior;
   110	- the request crosses a safety, authorization, destructive, privacy, or compatibility boundary;
   111	- the user outcome itself is unknown;
   112	- writing would create a second source for the same durable knowledge.

1	---
     2	name: add-idea
     3	description: >-
     4	  Unified, docs-only entry for adding a product or engineering idea to a
     5	  harness-managed repository. Use when the user invokes add-idea or asks to
     6	  turn an idea into a new Feature or a bounded change to an existing Feature.
     7	  Inspect current owners first, Grill unclear ideas one decision at a time,
     8	  then create or patch requirements, a Spec, and conditional ADRs without
     9	  implementing code or publishing external issues.
    10	disable-model-invocation: true
    11	---
    12	
    13	# Add Idea
    14	
    15	Use this as the single explicit intake for an idea. The outcome is a clear,
    16	routed internal contract, not code implementation.
    17	
    18	Read [references/routing-contract.md](references/routing-contract.md) completely
    19	before deciding the route. When writing durable artifacts, also read
    20	`../progressive-disclosure-docs/references/feature-spec-decision-contract.md`.
    21	
    22	## Invariants
    23	
    24	- Keep the original user outcome visible while refining details.
    25	- Investigate repository facts; ask the user only for decisions.
    26	- Ask one question at a time during Grill and include a recommended answer with
    27	  a short rationale.
    28	- Do not write Feature, requirements, Spec, or ADR docs until the user confirms
    29	  the final shared-understanding summary.
    30	- The agent chooses the owner route from evidence. Ask the user only when two or
    31	  more owners remain equally valid or the choice changes a product boundary.
    32	- This skill never grants code implementation, deployment, training, execution,
    33	  external publication, or issue-tracker actions.
    34	- Do not persist interview transcripts or a separate idea backlog. Confirmed
    35	  content must return to the existing Feature/requirements/Spec/ADR owners.
    36	
    37	## Workflow
    38	
    39	### 1. Discover the current ownership map
    40	
    41	Read progressively:
    42	
    43	1. root `AGENTS.md` or equivalent;
    44	2. `docs/OVERVIEW.md`;
    45	3. `docs/feature/INDEX.md`;
    46	4. at most the likely owning Feature README/INDEX and `requirements.md` files;
    47	5. targeted reference docs and code only when they can settle a fact.
    48	
    49	Record in the session:
    50	
    51	- the problem, actor, and intended outcome;
    52	- candidate Feature owners and supporting evidence;
    53	- existing expected behavior and current implementation;
    54	- safety, authorization, public-contract, and data boundaries;
    55	- facts already established and decisions still open.
    56	
    57	Do not create a new Feature merely because the user used a new phrase. Prefer an
    58	existing owner when its responsibility and lifecycle genuinely cover the idea.
    59	
    60	### 2. Apply the clarity gate
    61	
    62	An idea is ready for routing only when these are clear enough to distinguish
    63	ownership and acceptance:
    64	
    65	- problem and intended user/business outcome;
    66	- in-scope and out-of-scope behavior;
    67	- measurable acceptance or an observable completion condition;
    68	- relevant constraints, safety, authorization, and compatibility boundaries;
    69	- candidate owner and affected contracts;
    70	- unresolved decisions that would change the owner, public behavior, schema,
    71	  state ownership, migration, validation, or rollback.
    72	
    73	If route-affecting ambiguity remains, enter Grill. If all items are already
    74	clear from the request and repository, skip Grill and summarize the inferred
    75	boundary for confirmation.
    76	
    77	### 3. Grill unclear ideas
    78	
    79	Walk the unresolved decision tree in dependency order:
    80	
    81	1. Ask exactly one decision question.
    82	2. Give the recommended answer and why it best fits current evidence.
    83	3. Wait for the user's answer before advancing.
    84	4. Update the in-session decision ledger: confirmed facts, user decisions,
    85	   rejected alternatives, open questions, and affected owners.
    86	5. Look up newly discoverable facts instead of asking for them.
    87	
    88	Do not draft contracts while questions remain open. When all blocking branches
    89	are resolved, present one compact shared-understanding summary containing:
    90	
    91	- problem and outcome;
    92	- scope and non-goals;
    93	- acceptance and stop conditions;
    94	- selected owner and affected contracts;
    95	- durable decisions and remaining non-blocking unknowns;
    96	- recommended documentation route.
    97	
    98	Ask for explicit confirmation. Continue only after the user confirms the
    99	summary or corrects it.
   100	
   101	### 4. Choose two independent routes
   102	
   103	Choose one **owner route**:
   104	
   105	- `CREATE_FEATURE`: the idea needs an independent durable owner.
   106	- `PATCH_FEATURE`: exactly one existing Feature owns the behavior.
   107	- `BLOCKED_OWNER`: ownership remains ambiguous or conflicts with project
   108	  boundaries; stop and surface the competing owners.
   109	
   110	Then choose one or more **artifact routes**:
   111	
   112	- `REQUIREMENTS_PATCH`: expected behavior, acceptance, non-goals, constraints,
   113	  or stop rules change.
   114	- `NEW_SPEC`: implementation-relevant contracts change, including public API,
   115	  schema, state machine, module ownership, data flow, migration, compatibility,
   116	  security, validation, rollout, or rollback.
   117	- `ADR_CANDIDATE`: a durable architecture decision meets the decision trigger.
   118	- `STATE_ONLY`: only the Feature's durable current-state summary or routing
   119	  changes; do not invent requirements or a Spec.
   120	- `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE`: the idea is a reversible local detail with no expected
   121	  behavior, contract, decision, or durable state impact; report the owner and
   122	  stop without changing docs.
   123	
   124	`CREATE_FEATURE` and `NEW_SPEC` are not opposites. A new Feature normally starts
   125	with requirements and may also receive its first Spec. An existing Feature may
   126	receive a requirements patch, a new Spec, an ADR, or a combination.
   127	
   128	State the chosen routes and evidence before writing. Do not ask the user to pick
   129	between routes when the repository evidence is decisive.
   130	
   131	### 5. Materialize the confirmed contract
   132	
   133	Follow the shared Feature/Spec/ADR contract.
   134	
   135	For `CREATE_FEATURE`:
   136	
   137	- create the Feature from
   138	  `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/feature-template/`;
   139	- replace every placeholder with confirmed content;
   140	- after faithfully materializing the confirmed boundary, set requirements to
   141	  `CONFIRMED`, record the real confirmation date/authority when known, and
   142	  update README requirements/route status; do not leave initial `DRAFT`
   143	  scaffolding or a stale contract-freeze blocker;
   144	- register it in `docs/feature/INDEX.md` and `docs/OVERVIEW.md`;
   145	- keep Feature lifecycle separate from Spec delivery status.
   146	
   147	For `PATCH_FEATURE`:
   148	
   149	- update the existing owner in place;
   150	- set a changed requirements revision to `CONFIRMED` only when the confirmed
   151	  shared-understanding summary fully covers that revision; otherwise stop
   152	  rather than writing a partial contract;
   153	- preserve unrelated requirements and current-state content;
   154	- add a new Spec instead of overwriting a validated or superseded Spec;
   155	- update parent routes and back-links only when new artifacts are created.
   156	
   157	For artifact routes:
   158	
   159	- when `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE` applies, write no docs and explain why;
   160	- write expected behavior only to `requirements.md`;
   161	- create a Spec and lazy index from `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/spec-template.md` and `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/spec-index-template.md` when `NEW_SPEC` applies;
   162	- create an ADR and lazy index from `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/adr-template.md` and `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/decision-index-template.md` only when the ADR trigger applies;
   163	- keep ADR-worthy rationale out of README and keep implementation design out of
   164	  requirements;
   165	- update README with links and compact status only;
   166	- append the durable transition to `changelog.md`.
   167	
   168	A blocking ADR stays `proposed` until the decision authority accepts it. A Spec
   169	cannot become `frozen` while blocking decisions or contract questions remain.
   170	
   171	### 6. Stop at the documentation gate
   172	
   173	Finish with:
   174	
   175	- selected owner route and rationale;
   176	- artifact routes and files created or updated;
   177	- requirements, Spec, and decision statuses;
   178	- unresolved blockers;
   179	- next documentation or validation gate;
   180	- explicit statement that implementation remains unauthorized.
   181	
   182	Do not implement code in the same invocation. A later implementation request
   183	must enter `project-docs-workflow` and re-check the frozen contracts.
   184	
   185	## Stop conditions
   186	
   187	Stop without expanding the change when:
   188	
   189	- the user has not confirmed shared understanding;
   190	- no owner can be selected without changing a product boundary;
   191	- expected behavior conflicts with an existing frozen contract;
   192	- a blocking architecture decision is still unresolved;
   193	- the requested artifact would create a second SSOT;
   194	- the request crosses a safety, authorization, data, or external-publication
   195	  boundary that the user has not explicitly approved.

    81	1. Ask exactly one decision question.
    82	2. Give the recommended answer and why it best fits current evidence.
    83	3. Wait for the user's answer before advancing.
    84	4. Update the in-session decision ledger: confirmed facts, user decisions,
    85	   rejected alternatives, open questions, and affected owners.
    86	5. Look up newly discoverable facts instead of asking for them.
    87	
    88	Do not draft contracts while questions remain open. When all blocking branches
    89	are resolved, present one compact shared-understanding summary containing:
    90	
    91	- problem and outcome;
    92	- scope and non-goals;
    93	- acceptance and stop conditions;
    94	- selected owner and affected contracts;
    95	- durable decisions and remaining non-blocking unknowns;
    96	- recommended documentation route.
    97	
    98	Ask for explicit confirmation. Continue only after the user confirms the
    99	summary or corrects it.
   100	
   101	### 4. Choose two independent routes
   102	
   103	Choose one **owner route**:
   104	
   105	- `CREATE_FEATURE`: the idea needs an independent durable owner.
   106	- `PATCH_FEATURE`: exactly one existing Feature owns the behavior.
   107	- `BLOCKED_OWNER`: ownership remains ambiguous or conflicts with project
   108	  boundaries; stop and surface the competing owners.
   109	
   110	Then choose one or more **artifact routes**:
   111	
   112	- `REQUIREMENTS_PATCH`: expected behavior, acceptance, non-goals, constraints,
   113	  or stop rules change.
   114	- `NEW_SPEC`: implementation-relevant contracts change, including public API,
   115	  schema, state machine, module ownership, data flow, migration, compatibility,
   116	  security, validation, rollout, or rollback.
   117	- `ADR_CANDIDATE`: a durable architecture decision meets the decision trigger.
   118	- `STATE_ONLY`: only the Feature's durable current-state summary or routing
   119	  changes; do not invent requirements or a Spec.
   120	- `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE`: the idea is a reversible local detail with no expected
   121	  behavior, contract, decision, or durable state impact; report the owner and
   122	  stop without changing docs.
   123	
   124	`CREATE_FEATURE` and `NEW_SPEC` are not opposites. A new Feature normally starts
   125	with requirements and may also receive its first Spec. An existing Feature may
   126	receive a requirements patch, a new Spec, an ADR, or a combination.
   127	
   128	State the chosen routes and evidence before writing. Do not ask the user to pick
   129	between routes when the repository evidence is decisive.
   130	
   131	### 5. Materialize the confirmed contract
   132	
   133	Follow the shared Feature/Spec/ADR contract.
   134	
   135	For `CREATE_FEATURE`:
   136	
   137	- create the Feature from
   138	  `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/feature-template/`;
   139	- replace every placeholder with confirmed content;
   140	- after faithfully materializing the confirmed boundary, set requirements to
   141	  `CONFIRMED`, record the real confirmation date/authority when known, and
   142	  update README requirements/route status; do not leave initial `DRAFT`
   143	  scaffolding or a stale contract-freeze blocker;
   144	- register it in `docs/feature/INDEX.md` and `docs/OVERVIEW.md`;
   145	- keep Feature lifecycle separate from Spec delivery status.
   146	
   147	For `PATCH_FEATURE`:
   148	
   149	- update the existing owner in place;
   150	- set a changed requirements revision to `CONFIRMED` only when the confirmed
   151	  shared-understanding summary fully covers that revision; otherwise stop
   152	  rather than writing a partial contract;
   153	- preserve unrelated requirements and current-state content;
   154	- add a new Spec instead of overwriting a validated or superseded Spec;
   155	- update parent routes and back-links only when new artifacts are created.
   156	
   157	For artifact routes:
   158	
   159	- when `NO_DURABLE_CHANGE` applies, write no docs and explain why;
   160	- write expected behavior only to `requirements.md`;
   161	- create a Spec and lazy index from `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/spec-template.md` and `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/spec-index-template.md` when `NEW_SPEC` applies;
   162	- create an ADR and lazy index from `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/adr-template.md` and `../progressive-disclosure-docs/assets/decision-index-template.md` only when the ADR trigger applies;
   163	- keep ADR-worthy rationale out of README and keep implementation design out of
   164	  requirements;
   165	- update README with links and compact status only;
   166	- append the durable transition to `changelog.md`.
   167	
   168	A blocking ADR stays `proposed` until the decision authority accepts it. A Spec
   169	cannot become `frozen` while blocking decisions or contract questions remain.
   170	
   171	### 6. Stop at the documentation gate
   172	
   173	Finish with:
   174	
   175	- selected owner route and rationale;
   176	- artifact routes and files created or updated;
   177	- requirements, Spec, and decision statuses;
   178	- unresolved blockers;
   179	- next documentation or validation gate;
   180	- explicit statement that implementation remains unauthorized.
   181	
   182	Do not implement code in the same invocation. A later implementation request
   183	must enter `project-docs-workflow` and re-check the frozen contracts.
   184	
   185	## Stop conditions
   186	
   187	Stop without expanding the change when:
   188	
   189	- the user has not confirmed shared understanding;
   190	- no owner can be selected without changing a product boundary;
   191	- expected behavior conflicts with an existing frozen contract;
   192	- a blocking architecture decision is still unresolved;
   193	- the requested artifact would create a second SSOT;
   194	- the request crosses a safety, authorization, data, or external-publication
   195	  boundary that the user has not explicitly approved.

1	---
     2	name: project-docs-workflow
     3	description: >-
     4	  轻量项目文档编排。用于非 trivial 功能、bug、重构、API 或跨模块修改，以及用户询问当前路线、
     5	  进度、已实现行为或 expected-vs-implemented gap。开始时只读取少量相关 docs，优先完成任务，
     6	  验证结束后由主 Agent 异步委派一个 docs SubAgent，用一轮增量 patch 更新真正受影响的核心文档。
     7	  不要让附属文档维护阻塞主任务，也不要创建 Spec、平行进度文件或繁重门禁。
     8	---
     9	
    10	# 项目 Docs 工作流
    11	
    12	这是一个薄编排层：帮助 Agent 找到必要上下文，并在任务完成后维护长期文档。它不取代代码分析、
    13	项目测试或用户授权，也不要求每个任务产生文档。
    14	
    15	## 快速原则
    16	
    17	- 先做事，再整理长期文档。
    18	- 开工前只读，不写 docs。
    19	- 默认读取 1-3 份任务相关文档；缺少文档不自动阻塞实现。
    20	- 不要求 TDD、测试先行、Spec、固定状态机、验证矩阵或阶段性 changelog。
    21	- 只有目标或硬边界无法判断时才问用户；可逆细节沿用仓库惯例。
    22	- 完成实现和验证后，主 Agent 发起一个异步 docs 子任务，集中做一次影响判断和一次增量更新。
    23	- docs SubAgent 是该轮唯一文档 writer；主 Agent 不等待，也不再并发修改同一批 docs。
    24	
    25	## 何时使用
    26	
    27	适合：
    28	
    29	- 非 trivial 功能、bug 修复、重构、API 或跨模块修改；
    30	- 用户询问当前路线、进度、下一步或已实现行为；
    31	- 文档与代码可能不一致，需要判断长期知识是否应更新；
    32	- 外部建议已经被内部接受，准备在当前仓库中实施。
    33	
    34	通常跳过：
    35	
    36	- typo、格式调整、明确的单文件小修；
    37	- 纯搜索或临时分析；
    38	- 用户明确要求不改 docs；
    39	- 本次变化不产生长期可复用知识。
    40	
    41	## 工作流
    42	
    43	### 1. 读取最小上下文
    44	
    45	先读适用的 `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`，然后按项目现有结构选择：
    46	
    47	1. `docs/OVERVIEW.md`，如果存在且能帮助定位；
    48	2. owning Feature 的 `README.md` / `INDEX.md`；
    49	3. 一份直接相关的 reference、接口或运行文档；
    50	4. 当前代码入口和相关测试。
    51	
    52	不要为了遵循固定清单而创建缺失文件，也不要全量读取 `docs/`。文档是导航和历史上下文；当前代码
    53	决定已实现行为，用户明确要求决定本次目标。
    54	
    55	### 2. 只澄清真正阻塞的问题
    56	
    57	当下列核心内容无法从请求、代码或现有文档判断时，才询问用户：
    58	
    59	- 用户真正想要的结果；
    60	- 会改变产品边界的 scope 选择；
    61	- 安全、授权、数据损失、兼容性或不可逆迁移边界。
    62

1	---
     2	name: document-organization-harness
     3	description: >-
     4	  Organize or retrofit project documentation: author AGENTS.md, docs
     5	  overview/index maps, module documentation boundaries, owning GOAL/README
     6	  status routing, and progressive-disclosure documentation. Use when a
     7	  repository needs a clear documentation structure, navigation hierarchy, or
     8	  documentation governance.
     9	---
    10	
    11	# Document Organization Harness
    12	
    13	Use this skill when a repo needs a portable harness layer: a root instruction
    14	file, a navigable docs map, explicit module ownership, and a documentation tree
    15	an agent can follow without guessing the repo shape.
    16	
    17	## Outcome
    18	
    19	Deliver the smallest useful harness that still gives an agent clear entry points:
    20	
    21	- root `AGENTS.md` or equivalent
    22	- optional `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` for an always-applied contract,
    23	  validation, and documentation synchronization gate
    24	- `docs/OVERVIEW.md`
    25	- `docs/feature/INDEX.md`
    26	- `docs/reference/INDEX.md`
    27	- `docs/collaboration/INDEX.md`
    28	- `docs/archive/INDEX.md`
    29	- module-level `README.md` / `INDEX.md` plus `requirements.md` for expected
    30	  product or business behavior and acceptance
    31	- lazy `specs/` for bounded implementation contracts and `decisions/` for ADRs
    32	- owning GOAL/README sections for completed work, pending work, blockers, and
    33	  the next validation gate
    34	- leaf docs with explicit parent links
    35	
    36	## Workflow
    37	
    38	1. Inspect existing root instructions, docs, and ownership boundaries.
    39	2. Identify the repo's real layers before writing any new structure.
    40	3. Create or repair the docs map first; distinguish `requirements.md` for
    41	   expected behavior, Specs for bounded implementation contracts, ADRs for
    42	   durable rationale, and `README.md` / `INDEX.md` for current state/routing.
    43	4. Route durable progress through the owning GOAL/README instead of creating a
    44	   separate execution-control document.
    45	5. Write leaf docs only after the parent indexes exist.
    46	6. Record stable validation evidence in owning docs or append-only artifacts.
    47	7. Keep top-down discoverability and bottom-up traceability intact.
    48	8. Validate that an agent can start at `AGENTS.md`, find the next doc, and walk
    49	   back.
    50	
    51	## Rules
    52	
    53	- Treat docs as routing, not as a dumping ground.
    54	- Keep business content out of the harness layer.
    55	- Keep stack-specific details in repo-local adapters or references.
    56	- Prefer repairing an existing partial harness over replacing it.
    57	- Use root-relative links for deep cross-tree references.
    58	- Keep expected behavior, current implementation, current progress, and
    59	  historical evidence distinct, with each routed to its owning durable file.
    60	- Do not persist transient decomposition solely to coordinate the current
    61	  session; use the session's planning surface instead.
    62	- Before non-trivial implementation, freeze module owners, public interfaces,
    63	  dependency direction, mutable-state ownership, file budgets, and test ownership.
    64	- Keep new or changed handwritten files at or below 1000 physical lines; at
    65	  800 lines, review responsibility-based extraction with `refactor-large-modules`.
    66	- Delegation is never implied by this skill. When a user explicitly requests
    67	  delegation, use bounded owner scopes and isolated worktrees where needed.
    68	- **Enforcement must be runtime-injected, not just described.** In a Cursor
    69	  repo, keep the contract, validation, evidence, and documentation synchronization
    70	  gate in BOTH `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`) and
    71	  root `AGENTS.md`.
    72	
    73	## Reference
    74	
    75	Read `references/harness-bootstrap.md` for:
    76	
    77	- AGENTS.md section order
    78	- docs tree templates
    79	- sample feature module with README + requirements separation
    80	- owning GOAL/README status rules
    81	- leaf-document link rules
    82	- validation checklist
    83	- per-project skill maintenance and contract migration
    84	
    85	## Demo Pack
    86	
    87	If the target repo needs a fast bootstrap, adapt the included demo harness from
    88	`assets/demo-harness/` and replace every placeholder with target-project facts.
    89	The demo pack includes:
    90	
    91	- a root `AGENTS.md` with documentation governance and execution-safety rules
    92	- a Cursor-native `.cursor/rules/harness-execution.mdc` gate (`alwaysApply: true`)
    93	- the `docs/` entry points
    94	- reference docs for architecture, interfaces, and validation
    95	- one sample feature module showing README + requirements separation
    96	
    97	Use it as a starting shape, not as a final domain model.
    98	
    99	## Suite Maintenance Boundary
   100	
   101	This repository is the canonical maintenance source for independent harness skills. It does not
   102	provide a bundle manifest, installer, automatic overwrite, or target-project upgrade command.
   103	Projects may maintain the full suite, a subset, or local extensions in grouped or flat paths.
   104	
   105	`add-idea` is the explicit docs-only intake for unclear or clear product/engineering ideas. It runs
   106	the Grill protocol when needed, chooses a new or existing Feature owner, and materializes
   107	requirements, Specs, and conditional ADRs before later implementation workflows.
   108	
   109	Recommended maintenance flow:
   110	
   111	1. Read the suite [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) and
   112	   [`UPGRADING.md`](../UPGRADING.md).
   113	2. Inspect the target project's actual skill registry, layout, local extensions, and working tree.
   114	3. Compare and update only the individual skills the target uses; do not normalize paths or replace
   115	   directories containing unclassified local content.
   116	4. When adopting the full lifecycle change, maintain shared contracts first, then producer and
   117	   consumer skills, then patch target-owned governance.
   118	5. Follow the suite [`AGENTS.md` patch contract](../README.md) to incrementally update existing target
   119	   rules; never replace target-owned rules or Feature docs.
   120	
   121	See `references/harness-bootstrap.md` for docs scaffolding and maintenance order. Target repository
   122	history, reviewed diffs, and validation evidence remain the truth for what that project maintains.

1	---
     2	name: document-organization-harness
     3	description: >-
     4	  Organize or simplify project documentation: a short root agent rule, an optional docs overview,
     5	  lightweight feature/reference routing, and clear owners for stable knowledge. Use when a repository
     6	  needs a usable docs map, when an existing harness is too heavy, or when scattered Markdown needs a
     7	  smaller progressive-disclosure structure.
     8	---
     9	
    10	# Document Organization Harness
    11	
    12	Build the smallest documentation layer that helps an Agent work without guessing. A documentation harness should reduce
    13	reading and maintenance, not introduce a new project-management system.
    14	
    15	## Default Outcome
    16	
    17	Choose only the pieces the repository needs:
    18	
    19	- a short `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` section pointing to context;
    20	- `docs/OVERVIEW.md` when the project needs a module map;
    21	- `docs/feature/INDEX.md` when several Features need routing;
    22	- one `README.md` per durable Feature that needs its own owner;
    23	- `docs/reference/INDEX.md` and targeted references when stable cross-module facts need a home.
    24	
    25	Do not pre-create requirements, Specs, ADRs, changelogs, archives, collaboration directories, task boards, evidence
    26	ledgers, route manifests, or status schemas. Preserve any of these that the target project already uses effectively.
    27	
    28	## Workflow
    29	
    30	1. Inspect existing root instructions, docs entrypoints, and real code ownership.
    31	2. Identify duplicate, stale, or orphaned documentation and the documents people actually use.
    32	3. Design the smallest useful navigation path before editing.
    33	4. Prefer repairing existing files over replacing the tree.
    34	5. Apply the docs reorganization in one coherent patch after the inventory is complete.
    35	6. Verify that a normal task reaches its owner after reading no more than a few documents.
    36	7. Check affected links and report any intentionally retained legacy structure.
    37	
    38	## Rules
    39	
    40	- Treat overview and index files as maps, not full manuals.
    41	- Keep project-specific content in project-owned docs, not in generic harness rules.
    42	- Keep transient plans, analysis, raw logs, and current-session checklists out of long-term docs.
    43	- Put Feature-specific stable knowledge in its README; put stable cross-Feature facts in reference docs.
    44	- Split a document only when the split improves navigation or ownership. Do not use fixed line counts or document-count
    45	  thresholds as automatic triggers.
    46	- Update upper indexes only when navigation changes.
    47	- Do not duplicate the same rule in root instructions and runtime-specific rule files unless the target platform truly
    48	  requires both.
    49	- Do not imply worktrees, TDD, testing-first, or implementation authorization.
    50	- For implementation tasks, use one asynchronous docs SubAgent after completion; keep one writer and do not block the main Agent.
    51	- Reuse the target repository's existing tests and docs checks; do not invent commands.
    52	
    53	## Reference
    54	
    55	Read [`references/harness-bootstrap.md`](references/harness-bootstrap.md) for a lightweight bootstrap and migration guide.
    56	Use [`assets/demo-harness/`](assets/demo-harness/) only as a shape example. Remove every placeholder and every unused
    57	file instead of copying the pack wholesale.
    58	
    59	## Suite Maintenance
    60	
    61	This repository is the canonical source for independent harness skills. Target projects may maintain the full suite, a
    62	subset, or local extensions.
    63	
    64	1. Read [`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) and [`UPGRADING.md`](../UPGRADING.md).
    65	2. Inspect the target registry, layout, working tree, and local rules.
    66	3. Compare only the skills the target actually uses.
    67	4. Preserve target-owned safety, authorization, commands, and useful local conventions.
    68	5. Apply the lightweight docs rules only where they replace an accepted harness behavior.
    69	6. Validate the target-specific diff and links.
    70	
    71	Never replace a target `AGENTS.md`, docs tree, or skill directory wholesale when it contains unclassified local content.

50	3. `project-docs-workflow` asynchronous docs handoff;
    51	4. `project-analysis` and external collaboration consumers;
    52	5. `document-organization-harness` bootstrap/demo;
    53	6. target-owned root or runtime rules.
    54	
    55	A partial installation may update only the surfaces it uses. Remove links to absent skills or references.
    56	
    57	### 4. Patch Target Governance
    58	
    59	Preserve project safety, authorization, ownership, commands, and useful local conventions. Add only the accepted behavior:
    60	
    61	- read a few relevant docs instead of the whole tree;
    62	- do not create documentation as a start gate;
    63	- do not prescribe TDD, testing-first, fixed status machines, or typed implementation-contract lifecycles;
    64	- finish implementation and risk-matched validation first;
    65	- then have the main Agent asynchronously delegate one bounded docs update to a single SubAgent writer;
    66	- do not make the main Agent wait for ancillary docs maintenance;
    67	- ask the user only about the desired outcome or a hard boundary that cannot be inferred safely.
    68	
    69	When the environment has no SubAgent, retain a one-pass main-Agent fallback at task completion.
    70	
    71	## Migrating Older Harness Docs
    72	
    73	Do not bulk-delete working project knowledge. Migrate when related work touches it or when the user requests cleanup:
    74	
    75	1. Identify stable content in legacy requirements, implementation-contract, decision, changelog, route-manifest, or
    76	   status-matrix documents.
    77	2. Move only still-useful Feature knowledge into the owning Feature README.
    78	3. Move stable cross-Feature architecture, interfaces, or runbook content into existing references.
    79	4. Keep a legacy document when it still has a real audience or project-owned purpose.
    80	5. Remove obsolete files only after active links and agent rules no longer depend on them.
    81	6. Update navigation once after the migration patch.
    82	
    83	Do not convert old typed docs into a new set of typed docs. The goal is fewer owners and lower ongoing maintenance.
    84	
    85	## Validation
    86	
    87	After each target update:
    88	
    89	- review the diff and preserve unrelated work;
    90	- validate skill frontmatter and provider metadata;
    91	- check registered paths and active documentation links;
    92	- confirm root and runtime rules do not contradict each other;
    93	- confirm one asynchronous docs writer is used after task completion and the main Agent is not required to wait;
    94	- confirm old start gates and dead template links are gone;
    95	- run the target project's existing docs/lint checks and `git diff --check`.
    96	
    97	## Rollback
    98	
    99	Keep the target change reviewable. Roll back through the target project's normal version-control process, restoring skill
   100	files and governance references together so no registry path points to a removed file.
   101	
   102	## Multiple Projects
   103	
   104	Upgrade a small representative target first. Record which skills were updated, which local behavior was preserved,
   105	validation results, and rollback status. There is intentionally no central installation marker; target history remains
   106	the source of truth.

1	# Mainline Route and Cognitive Disclosure Contract
     2	
     3	Use this reference when the user changes or asks about the project mainline, execution route,
     4	parallel workstreams, inserted stages, current progress, blockers, or next step.
     5	
     6	This is a shared contract, not a standalone route-management skill. `project-docs-workflow`
     7	orchestrates the full loop; `project-analysis` is only an escalation for real dependency, join,
     8	contract, evidence, or authorization ambiguity.
     9	
    10	## Ownership stack
    11	
    12	```text
    13	AGENTS.md             stable collaboration and output rules
    14	  -> OVERVIEW.md      single current-Feature pointer
    15	    -> README.md      current route overlay and macro roll-up
    16	      -> development-plan.md  stable DAG, dependencies and gates
    17	      -> child GOALs           local workstream progress
    18	        -> code/artifacts      implementation and evidence detail
    19	```
    20	
    21	- Do not copy current route state into AGENTS, OVERVIEW or Feature indexes.
    22	- Keep current-turn ordering in the session plan.
    23	- Append durable route transitions to the owning changelog.
    24	
    25	## Route operations
    26	
    27	| User intent | Normalized operation | Durable write |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| A then B | `A -> B` | README; development plan if dependency changed |
    30	| A and B together | `A || B` | README + development plan + changelog |
    31	| join after A/B | `[A || B] -> J` | README + development plan + changelog |
    32	| insert X | `A -> X -> B` | README + development plan + changelog |
    33	| do B first this turn | focus only | session plan |
    34	| pause/drop/replace a node | explicit mutation | README + development plan + changelog |
    35	| switch current Feature | project pointer mutation | OVERVIEW + old/new owners + changelog |
    36	
    37	The letters above are abstract machine notation, not user-facing labels. Use stable, unique node IDs
    38	internally and give every node a semantic `name` taken from the owning module or milestone. A name may
    39	change; a retired ID must not be reassigned.
    40	
    41	## README manifest
    42	
    43	Place one hidden JSON block in every active Feature README:
    44	
    45	```markdown
    46	<!-- MAINLINE-ROUTE:START
    47	{
    48	  "schema_version": 2,
    49	  "route_version": "YYYY-MM-DD.N",
    50	  "summary": "合同冻结已完成 → [观测工程进行中 ∥ 模拟器工程已准备] → 集成验证 → 模型训练未授权",
    51	  "nodes": [
    52	    {"id": "a", "name": "合同冻结", "progress": "passed", "authorization": "completed-scope", "owner": "README.md"},
    53	    {"id": "b", "name": "观测工程", "progress": "active", "authorization": "authorized", "owner": "b-goal.md"},
    54	    {"id": "c", "name": "模拟器工程", "progress": "prepared", "authorization": "authorized", "owner": "c-goal.md"},
    55	    {"id": "join", "name": "集成验证", "progress": "planned", "authorization": "authorized", "owner": "development-plan.md"},
    56	    {"id": "d", "name": "模型训练", "progress": "planned", "authorization": "unauthorized", "owner": "development-plan.md"}
    57	  ],
    58	  "edges": [["a", "b"], ["a", "c"], ["b", "join"], ["c", "join"], ["join", "d"]],
    59	  "focus_nodes": ["b", "c"],
    60	  "parallel_groups": [["b", "c"]],
    61	  "joins": [{"id": "join", "requires": ["b", "c"]}],
    62	  "next_gate": "join"
    63	}
    64	MAINLINE-ROUTE:END -->
    65	```
    66	
    67	Immediately below it, render the exact `summary` in one visible route line, followed by at most:
    68	current focus, blocker, next gate, authorization boundary, and links to child owners.
    69	Every user-visible field must use semantic module/milestone names. Keep raw node IDs, phase codes,
    70	and shorthand such as `M0`, `M3C`, or `A/BC` inside the manifest or implementation docs unless the
    71	user explicitly asks for them.
    72	
    73	When a node owner is a child `*-goal.md`, keep one hidden roll-up state in that GOAL:
    74	
    75	```markdown
    76	<!-- ROUTE-NODE:START
    77	{"id":"b","progress":"active","authorization":"authorized"}
    78	ROUTE-NODE:END -->
    79	```
    80	
    81	The child GOAL remains the detailed owner. The parent README carries only the same node ID, progress,
    82	and authorization as a macro roll-up; update both in one change whenever any of those three values moves.
    83	
    84	## Output levels
    85	
    86	- **L0 — default**: goal, route, current focus, blocker, next gate, authorization, all expressed with semantic module/milestone names. No implementation inventory or internal IDs.
    87	- **L1 — expand one workstream**: local STEP, dependency, completion condition, blocker and next action.
    88	- **L2 — implementation/evidence**: files, interfaces, tests, commands and artifacts only when requested or necessary.
    89	
    90	When a user asks for progress without specifying depth, always return L0. When route interpretation is
    91	unambiguous, state the normalized route briefly and proceed. Ask only if an alternative interpretation
    92	would change dependency, contract, evidence meaning or authorization.
    93	
    94	## Validation expectations
    95	
    96	Validate one manifest per active owner, unique node IDs, non-empty semantic node names, existing owner paths, valid edge endpoints,
    97	an acyclic graph, valid focus/parallel/join references, explicit join edges, one next gate matching
    98	README metadata, an identical visible summary, child-GOAL roll-up consistency, and no copied
    99	manifest/summary in upper routing docs.

1	# Lightweight Mainline Route Guide
     2	
     3	Use this guide only when a project needs a development route to survive across sessions. Most tasks need only the
     4	session plan and no durable route update.
     5	
     6	## Owner
     7	
     8	Keep a short route or current-focus section in the owning Feature README. Use a separate development-plan document only
     9	when several durable workstreams and dependencies would make the README hard to scan.
    10	
    11	Do not create a route manifest, machine node IDs, status axes, or append-only route log by default.
    12	
    13	## Useful Content
    14	
    15	A durable route usually needs only:
    16	
    17	```text
    18	Goal: <durable outcome>
    19	Current focus: <semantic module or milestone>
    20	Next: <next meaningful step>
    21	Blocked by: <none or real dependency>
    22	```
    23	
    24	Use readable module and milestone names. Describe parallel work or joins in plain text when they matter.
    25	
    26	## Update Timing
    27	
    28	- Keep current-turn ordering in the session plan.
    29	- Update the durable route only when cross-session focus or dependencies genuinely change.
    30	- For implementation tasks, make that update in the single docs pass after implementation and validation complete.
    31	- Do not write progress after every command, file, test, or subtask.
    32	
    33	## Clarification
    34	
    35	Ask the user only when two route choices produce materially different outcomes, ownership, cost, or risk. If the order is
    36	reversible and does not affect a hard boundary, select a reasonable sequence and proceed.
    37	
    38	## Reporting
    39	
    40	When asked for progress, answer directly with the goal, current focus, blocker, and next step. Add implementation detail
    41	only when the user asks for it or when it explains a blocker.
